_comment: VQA subset of Stanford's CheXinstruct instruction-tuning collection (Stanford-AIMI/CheXagent). CheXinstruct itself aggregates ~28 source datasets via per-source 'processor' classes that all emit one unified record schema (unique_id, study_id, data_source, task_name, image_path, text, target_text, qa_pair, optional options). This integration covers only the two VQA-task processors whose images are exclusively MIMIC-CXR: MIMICCXRVQAProcessor (Open-Ended VQA, Close-Ended VQA) and MIMICDiffVQAProcessor (Difference VQA). The other five CheXinstruct VQA sources (VQA-RAD, SLAKE, MedVQA-2019, PMC-VQA, Rad-Restruct) are out of scope for this pass -- they'd each need their own image root, breaking the single-base_image_dir convention. Stanford's processor code (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, no derivatives) is run unmodified, offline, outside this repo, to produce a single compiled JSON; this harmonizer only reads that JSON and translates Stanford's schema into RadHarmony's BaseVQAHarmonizer schema -- it is original code, not a derivative of theirs.

primary_csv._comment: Not a CSV -- a compiled JSON produced by scripts/compile_chexinstruct_vqa.py, which runs the vendored, unmodified Stanford processors over MIMIC-CXR-VQA and MIMIC-Diff-VQA raw annotation releases. One row per QA sample, flattened across train/val/test with a 'split' field added.

patient_id._comment: Not a column in the compiled JSON. Every image_path already follows MIMIC-CXR-JPG's p../p<subject_id>/s<study_id>/<dicom>.jpg layout (Stanford's processors build it from the same mimic-cxr-2.0.0-metadata.csv RadHarmony's own MIMICCXRJPGHarmonizer uses), so subject_id is regex-extracted from image_path rather than joined from elsewhere.
patient_id.derivation: regex r'/p(\d+)/s\d+/' on image_path -> subject_id, cast to str

study_id._comment: Present as Stanford's own study_id field but wrapped, e.g. '[mimic-cxr] [50414267]'. Stripped to the bare numeric id so it matches MIMICCXRJPGHarmonizer's study_id format exactly (both are the plain MIMIC-CXR study_id as a string).
study_id.derivation: regex r'\[mimic-cxr\] \[(\d+)\]' on the raw study_id string

image_path._comment: Stanford's image_path is 'data/mimic-cxr/files/p../p.../s.../<dicom>.jpg' (a list of one path for MIMIC-Diff-VQA, a plain string for MIMIC-CXR-VQA). Stripping the 'data/mimic-cxr/files/' prefix lands exactly on RadHarmony's existing MIMIC-CXR-JPG base_image_dir -- no new image root needed.
image_path.derivation: unwrap single-element list (MIMIC-Diff-VQA) or use string directly (MIMIC-CXR-VQA)

labels._comment: Not applicable -- this is a VQA harmonizer (BaseVQAHarmonizer), not a classification harmonizer. No LABEL_COLS.

view_position._comment: Not supported/not applicable for this VQA dataset.

reports._comment: Not applicable -- these are QA pairs (question/answer), not reports.

extra_init_params._comment: VQA-schema-specific fields carried through beyond the BaseVQAHarmonizer core columns, plus constructor-level subset filters.
extra_init_params.question_type: task_name from the compiled JSON: 'Open-Ended VQA', 'Close-Ended VQA', or 'Difference VQA'.
extra_init_params.answer_struct: the 'options' dict (e.g. {'yes': true, 'no': false}) present on close-ended rows only; null/absent for open-ended and difference rows.
extra_init_params.data_source: kept as an EXTRA_OUTPUT_COLS column ('MIMIC-CXR-VQA' or 'MIMIC-Diff-VQA') for provenance.
extra_init_params.question_types: optional list[str], subset/combination of QUESTION_TYPES to keep; filters before the per-row patient_id/study_id parsing for efficiency on the ~700k-row compiled file.
extra_init_params.data_sources: optional list[str], subset/combination of DATA_SOURCES to keep.
extra_init_params.source_image_dirs: optional dict[str, str] mapping data_source -> image root, for per-source roots. base_image_dir is shorthand for one root shared by every source (today's actual case -- both sources are MIMIC-CXR-derived); source_image_dirs takes precedence and is the general form future CheXinstruct families with multiple roots will need.

custom_preprocessing: Requires running scripts/compile_chexinstruct_vqa.py, which runs the vendored processors (unmodified Stanford processor code, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) on locally-obtained MIMIC-CXR-VQA and MIMIC-Diff-VQA raw releases before this harmonizer has anything to read. See docs/wiki/reference/datasets/vqa-text/chexinstruct_vqa.md for the full data-acquisition steps.

expected_stats._comment: Checked by tests/test_dataset_stats.py. Source: compiled/chexinstruct_vqa.json read with pandas (701,458 questions). The table has one row per question, so rows is the question count (D-03). The patient ID comes from the /p<subject_id>/ part of the image path. The two sources made their splits on their own, so the official splits share 2,007 patients: 1,500 are in train and val, 495 in train and test, 10 in val and test, and 2 in all three. 663 of them come from the MIMIC-CXR-VQA split alone (train and val). MIMIC-Diff-VQA alone shares none.
